statement: Temporal evidence leakage and version contamination are different failure modes and their base rates are not interchangeable. Leakage is an availability, or transaction-time, violation: it asks whether an item was public at the as-of date, so it is violated only by evidence that is too new and is never violated by old evidence. Version contamination is a valid-time error about which version governs: it is violated both by superseded versions (too old) and by not-yet-in-force versions (too new). The two overlap only in the not-yet-in-force direction; the superseded direction that dominates amended-clause retrieval has no counterpart in the leakage metric, and leakage is defined over evidence availability rather than over competition between near-duplicate versions of the same clause. Therefore the 10.8% leakage figure cannot calibrate a version-contamination threshold, and the Stage-0 stop/go threshold must be justified by the oracle-gate headroom or by an independently measured baseline rather than by that prior.
